claim_boundary: Each result verifies that one exact public statement appeared in the fetched NIST SP 800-63-4 Digital Identity Guidelines bytes on 2026-08-04. It does not independently establish the statement's underlying real-world truth.

records.public_claim_text: Preface This publication and its companion volumes — [SP800-63A], [SP800-63B], and [SP800-63C] — provide technical and process guidelines to organizations for the implementation of digital identity services.
records.public_claim_verbatim_quote: Preface This publication and its companion volumes — [SP800-63A], [SP800-63B], and [SP800-63C] — provide technical and process guidelines to organizations for the implementation of digital identity services.

records.public_claim_text: When confidence in a person’s real-life identity is not required to provide access to an online service, organizations can use anonymous or pseudonymous accounts.
records.public_claim_verbatim_quote: When confidence in a person’s real-life identity is not required to provide access to an online service, organizations can use anonymous or pseudonymous accounts.

records.public_claim_text: In all other use cases, a digital identity is intended to establish trust between the holder of the digital identity and the person, organization, or system interacting with the online service.
records.public_claim_verbatim_quote: In all other use cases, a digital identity is intended to establish trust between the holder of the digital identity and the person, organization, or system interacting with the online service.

records.public_claim_text: The composition, models, and availability of identity services have significantly changed since the first version of SP 800-63 was released, as have the considerations and challenges of deploying secure, private, and usable services to users.
records.public_claim_verbatim_quote: The composition, models, and availability of identity services have significantly changed since the first version of SP 800-63 was released, as have the considerations and challenges of deploying secure, private, and usable services to users.

records.public_claim_text: Additionally, this publication provides instruction for credential service providers (CSPs), verifiers, and relying parties (RPs), to supplement the NIST Risk Management Framework [NISTRMF] and its component publications.
records.public_claim_verbatim_quote: Additionally, this publication provides instruction for credential service providers (CSPs), verifiers, and relying parties (RPs), to supplement the NIST Risk Management Framework [NISTRMF] and its component publications.

records.public_claim_text: Online services not covered by these guidelines include those associated with national security systems as defined in [44 U.S.C. § 3552(b)(6)].
records.public_claim_verbatim_quote: Online services not covered by these guidelines include those associated with national security systems as defined in [44 U.S.C. § 3552(b)(6)].

records.public_claim_text: SP 800-63 is organized as the following suite of volumes: • SP 800-63 Digital Identity Guidelines describes the digital identity models, risk assessment methodology, and processes for selecting assurance levels for identity proofing, authentication, and federation.
records.public_claim_verbatim_quote: SP 800-63 is organized as the following suite of volumes: • SP 800-63 Digital Identity Guidelines describes the digital identity models, risk assessment methodology, and processes for selecting assurance levels for identity proofing, authentication, and federation.

records.public_claim_text: SP 800-63A contains both normative and informative material. • [SP800-63B] provides requirements for authentication processes that can be used at each of the three AALs, including choices of authenticators.
records.public_claim_verbatim_quote: SP 800-63A contains both normative and informative material. • [SP800-63B] provides requirements for authentication processes that can be used at each of the three AALs, including choices of authenticators.

records.public_claim_text: SP 800-63B contains both normative and informative material. • [SP800-63C] provides requirements on the use of federated identity architectures and assertions to convey the results of authentication processes and relevant identity information to an organization’s application.
records.public_claim_verbatim_quote: SP 800-63B contains both normative and informative material. • [SP800-63C] provides requirements on the use of federated identity architectures and assertions to convey the results of authentication processes and relevant identity information to an organization’s application.

records.public_claim_text: Federal agencies implementing these guidelines are required to meet statutory responsibilities, including those under the Federal Information Security Modernization Act (FISMA) of 2014 [FISMA] and related NIST standards and guidelines.
records.public_claim_verbatim_quote: Federal agencies implementing these guidelines are required to meet statutory responsibilities, including those under the Federal Information Security Modernization Act (FISMA) of 2014 [FISMA] and related NIST standards and guidelines.
